tasks.short: Mark quizzes, read lab reports and papers, write feedback comments, decide grades, and enter grades in the spreadsheet and records system.

steps.what: Biology lecturer marks quizzes and closed questions by hand
Biology lecturer reads students' laboratory work and papers
Biology lecturer writes feedback comments to evaluate assignments

loop.input: The report, the rubric and the lecturer's short notes per rubric item.
loop.output: Draft feedback comments per rubric item, each quoting the passage it refers to.
loop.check: Code drops any comment whose quoted passage is not in the report; the lecturer checks that each quoted passage supports the point made and matches their own note, and edits every comment; unclear comments are rewritten by hand; no score is proposed.
loop.stop: One draft per report; stop when a rubric item lacks a quoted passage and leave that item to the lecturer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments must refer to each student's own work; fixed comment banks read as generic.

steps.what: Biology lecturer decides the grades
Biology lecturer enters grades: in a spreadsheet and the records system today, in the gradebook after the change
Biology lecturer checks the final grade list and feedback per student: each grade matches the decision and each comment belongs to that student's work
Biology lecturer releases the checked grades and feedback to students and the student records system

tasks.design: Quizzes and closed questions are marked by fixed answer keys in the learning system ({LMS}). For lab reports and papers, a bounded step drafts feedback comments from the lecturer's short notes per rubric item; comments that do not quote the report are dropped, the lecturer checks that each quote supports the comment, and edits every comment. The lecturer decides every grade; the gradebook computes totals and syncs to the student records system instead of a spreadsheet; the lecturer checks grades and feedback per student and releases them once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quizzes were marked by hand, comments typed in full and grades kept in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems mark closed questions and draft feedback from instructor notes.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can be generic on unusual lab results.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a careful method behind a failed experiment.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer edits feedback and decides grades instead of marking and typing.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
At the University of Michigan, assistants edited FeedbackWriter's rubric suggestions on 1,366 essays, agreed with 88% of its judgements, and revisions were better; no time data.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk; duties apply from 2 December 2027.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: from work submitted to grades entered; appeals are outside.
Input contract: rubric per assignment; fallback is writing comments in full.
The lecturer decides every grade; the tool proposes no scores.
A DPIA and the examination board's consent come before use.
s5, s5b and s5c are part of keeping grade records, which sibling task 25-1042.00:5805 covers; their saving is counted there, so they keep their full time here.
s3 keeps 70: the drafts save typing standard phrasing, but the lecturer's notes carry the content and every comment is checked and edited.
research_questions: How much of each drafted comment is kept?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer compares a sample of drafted comments with own reading.

approvals.approved_version: The grades and feedback per student exactly as checked by the lecturer in s5b, released once to students in the learning system and to the student records system; any change needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most drafted comments need rewriting, so s3 keeps 90 (14.5); high: drafts usable after editing as assumed (18.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search for recent findings, update lecture slides, deliver lectures on biology topics, and answer students' questions after lectures.

steps.what: Biology lecturer searches journals for recent findings to prepare lectures
Biology lecturer updates lecture slides
Biology lecturer delivers lectures to undergraduate or graduate students
Biology lecturer answers students' questions about lectures by e-mail

tasks.design: Saved searches and table-of-contents alerts in the citation databases ({OTHER}) bring new findings in the lecture topics, so journals are not searched one by one. Questions after lectures go to a course forum with a pinned FAQ ({LMS}), where students also answer each other. Updating slides and lecturing stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Journals were searched one by one and the same questions answered by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Citation databases send alerts; learning systems host forums.
tasks.still_hard: Students prefer private e-mail for some questions.
tasks.human_edge: Making a hard molecular mechanism click for a full hall.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and fewer repeated questions; lecturing stays.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lecture due to questions answered; exams are outside.
Input contract: library licences the databases; fallback is checking journals.
Students read the FAQ before asking; a little student time is priced.

incremental.description: Biology lecturer keeps the FAQ current.
Students read the FAQ and forum before asking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few students use the forum and FAQ, so answering mail keeps 90 (7.0); high: forum and FAQ take most repeated questions as assumed (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect course evaluations and pass rates, discuss revisions with colleagues and the programme committee, map learning outcomes to courses and assessments, and write the revised course plan.

steps.what: Biology lecturer collects course evaluation results and pass rates to evaluate curricula
Biology lecturer discusses revisions of course content with colleagues and the programme committee
Biology lecturer maps learning outcomes to courses and assessments: in a spreadsheet today, by linking them in the curriculum module after the change
Biology lecturer writes the revised course description and plan

tasks.design: A course dashboard ({BI}) shows evaluation scores, pass rates per assessment and trends over years, so results are not collected in spreadsheets. Learning outcomes are linked to courses and assessments in the curriculum module of the learning system ({LMS}), which shows gaps and overlaps. The revised course description starts from the catalogue entry. Discussing revisions stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were collected by hand and outcome maps kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Course dashboards and curriculum mapping modules are available.
tasks.still_hard: Older courses have no outcome links.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which topic to drop to make room for a new field.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer discusses and decides instead of compiling.

evidence.claim: Course dashboards and curriculum mapping modules can show results and outcome links.
Dashboards per examiner can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course review to the plan written; programme approval is outside.
Input contract: outcomes linked in the learning system; fallback is spreadsheets.

Discussions do not get shorter. s1 keeps 40 for reading the dashboard. s3 keeps 70: the lecturer still decides each link; the gap and overlap view replaces scanning the matrix by eye. s4 keeps 70 because the catalogue entry gives the standard parts and the lecturer writes the changes.
research_questions: Do outcome gaps get found earlier?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer keeps outcome links current when courses or assessments change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: outcomes are not linked in the learning system, so mapping stays in spreadsheets (18.5); high: the module is used as assumed (24.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write lab protocols and instructions, prepare material lists for practicals, write homework assignments and handouts, check the materials, and upload them for students.

steps.what: Biology lecturer prepares materials for laboratory activities such as protocols and instructions
Biology lecturer prepares reagent and equipment lists for practicals
Biology lecturer checks the final material list: reagents, equipment and quantities fit the protocol and the number of groups
Biology lecturer sends the checked material list to the lab technician
Biology lecturer writes homework assignments and handouts

loop.input: The learning outcomes, the week's lecture topics and earlier assignments.
loop.check: Any reference in the draft must resolve to the course list, a DOI or the library catalogue, else it is dropped; the lecturer checks that each item fits the outcome and that the cited source says what the item claims, and edits every item; unclear items are written by hand.
loop.stop: One draft per item; if rejected, the lecturer writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each assignment must fit the week's topics; a template gives only the frame.

steps.what: Biology lecturer checks the final course materials: protocols match the practical and assignments fit the outcomes
Biology lecturer releases the checked materials to students: uploading each file today, by one scheduled release in the learning system after the change

tasks.design: Lab protocols are kept as versioned templates in a protocol library ({DOCS}) and adapted per practical. Reagent and equipment lists are generated from the protocols and the number of student groups, so they are not built by hand; the lecturer checks each list and sends it once to the lab technician. A bounded step drafts homework and handouts from the outcomes and topics; unresolvable references are dropped, and the lecturer checks each item against the outcome and its source and edits it. Once checked, the lecturer releases materials to students in one scheduled release from the learning system ({LMS}).
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols, material lists and assignments were written or retyped each year.
tasks.enabler_now: Protocol libraries generate material lists; university chat platforms draft teaching texts.
tasks.still_hard: New practicals need full protocols and safety checks.
tasks.human_edge: Designing a practical where students find something they did not expect.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer edits and selects instead of retyping.

evidence.claim: EduGenAI is a university chat platform in pilot for teachers.
Drafting course materials is not a high-risk use under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from the practical planned to materials published; buying reagents is outside.
Input contract: protocols in the library with quantities per group; fallback is writing by hand.

The lecturer checks every item before release. s1 keeps 70 and s3 keeps 70: templates and drafts save layout and standard parts, the lecturer writes the rest. s2 keeps 50 for checking generated quantities. s5 keeps 10 for setting the release.
research_questions: Do material shortages in practicals fall?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer enters quantities per group in the protocols.

approvals.approved_version: The protocols, assignments and handouts exactly as checked by the lecturer in s4, released once to students in the learning system on the set date; any change needs a new check.
The material list with reagents, equipment and quantities exactly as checked by the lecturer in s2b, sent once to the lab technician for this practical; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: protocols are not kept in the library with quantities, so protocols and material lists are written by hand (17.0); high: library and drafts as assumed (35.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The biology lecturer keeps lecturing, judging lab work, deciding grades and revising courses with colleagues; hand marking, typed comments, compiling results and retyped materials shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer with more time for students and research.
